name: Empirical rule (68-95-99.7 rule)
subject: statistics
statement: For approximately normal data, about 68% of values lie within 1 SD of the mean, about 95% within 2 SD, and about 99.7% within 3 SD.
explanation: A rule of thumb derived from the normal curve; not valid for skewed data or heavy outliers.

proof.summary: Follows from integrating the normal density (beyond secondary level).

diagramRequirements: Bell curve with shaded 1, 2, 3 SD bands

application.problem: Test scores approx normal, mean 70, SD 4. What percent lie above 78?
application.solution: 78 is 2 SD above the mean; 95% lie within 2 SD, so 5% lie outside, half above: 2.5%.

verification.notes: Four fetched pages from three sites agree on 68/95/99.7 and the 'approximately normal' condition.

name: Central limit theorem (enrichment)
subject: statistics
statement: For samples of size n from a population with mean μ and SD σ, the distribution of the sample mean tends toward a normal with mean μ and SD σ/√n as n grows.
explanation: Explains why normal models appear for averages. College-level; enrichment only.
diagramRequirements: Histograms of sample means for n = 1, 5, 30

application.problem: σ = 12, n = 36: SD of the sample mean?

name: Law of total probability
subject: probability
statement: If A_1,…,A_n partition the sample space, then P(B) = ΣP(A_i)P(B|A_i).
conditions: Partition is mutually exclusive and exhaustive
explanation: Add the weighted branch probabilities of a tree diagram that end in B.

proof.summary: B is the disjoint union of the sets B ∩ A_i, each with probability P(A_i)P(B|A_i).

verification.notes: MathWorld equation (7) within Bayes derivation; Math is Fun tree example only.

name: Bayes' theorem
subject: probability
statement: P(A|B) = P(A)P(B|A)/P(B); with a partition, P(A_i|B) = P(A_i)P(B|A_i)/ΣP(A_j)P(B|A_j).
conditions: Partition if using the sum form
explanation: Reverses the direction of a conditional probability.

proof.summary: Equate P(A∩B) = P(A)P(B|A) = P(B)P(A|B) and divide by P(B).

name: Fundamental counting principle
subject: probability
statement: If one stage can occur in m ways and, for each, a second stage in n ways, the two stages together occur in m×n ways.

proof.summary: Tree of choices: m branches each splitting into n.

verification.notes: OpenStax Precalculus; Math is Fun partial.
